items.title: Pay 'Abschlag' to newly announced bank account (likely fraudulent)
items.quote: Bitte überweisen Sie den fälligen Abschlag von 214,00 € bis spätestens 11.09.2026.
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date, '11.09.2026', as the payment deadline; no period calculation is needed since a concrete date is given. However, strong indicators (see warnings) suggest this letter is a phishing/fraud attempt impersonating Stadtwerke Musterstadt, so this 'deadline' and the bank details should not be trusted or acted on without independent verification.

warnings: The IBAN given for the 'new' bank account (DE61 2004 1111 0512 3456 78) fails the standard IBAN checksum check, meaning it is not even a validly formed German IBAN — a strong sign of fraud.

The account holder for the new IBAN is named 'Global Energy Payments s.r.o.', which does not match the sender 'Stadtwerke Musterstadt' at all — legitimate utilities do not suddenly switch to a differently-named payee, especially not a foreign (s.r.o. = Czech/Slovak) company.

The letter uses classic scam pressure tactics: an urgent, very short deadline (4 days from the letter's own date) and a threat to cut off electricity 'ohne weitere Ankündigung' (without further notice) if not paid in time.

The letter tells the recipient not to reply in writing and to call only a given mobile 'special number' instead of the utility's normal customer service line, and its reply address 'kundenservice-mail.example' is not a genuine Stadtwerke domain — both are typical ways scammers prevent verification through known, trusted channels.

Do not transfer any money using the bank details in this letter; instead verify the alleged bank-account change directly with Stadtwerke Musterstadt using contact details from a previous genuine bill, contract, or their official website, not the phone number or email printed in this letter.
As of today (2026-09-26) the printed payment date of 11.09.2026 has already passed; this is noted only for completeness and is not a reason to pay now given the fraud indicators above.
